what: String literals in messages hold a run of 14 or more spaces: the `\` at a line's end and the newline were deleted and the next line's indentation kept, so the message prints with a gap and a test that asserts its text fails. Each was already so in the commit that first added it (six commits by six lanes, 2026-11-10 to 11-12): no mass edit did it.
cost: about ten messages printed wrong; one contracts test red; a lane's time to rule out a mass edit
cause: not traced; the shape (the space before the `\` plus the next line's indent, exactly) is what a non-raw Python string does to `\`-newline, as when an agent applies an edit with `python3 - <<'EOF' ... s.replace("""old""", """new""")`
class: source text passed through a layer that interprets escapes before it reaches the file
prevention: edit Rust source with the Edit tool or a raw string (r""".."""), never a non-raw Python string or an unquoted heredoc; a blaze lint that refuses a run of 8 or more spaces between two word or punctuation characters on one line of a non-raw string literal (pattern for string tokens: crates/blaze-lints/src/blaze/error_debug.rs:367), with a reasoned allow for the eight usage tables that align on purpose
workaround: find them: python3 -I <scratchpad>/scan.py 8 . crates fuzz harness scripts tools, or git grep -nE '[a-zA-Z.,:;)`(]  {14,}[a-zA-Z&(`{]' (which also matches aligned tables)
